<a name="web"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Web

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Web
```

Source: [framework/core/Web.php:22](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Web.php#L22)

Class Web (2.21.0)
A capability declared #[Capability(..., webOnly: true)] and served by Route::action() may return one of these
instead of plain data, to choose what the browser gets:

```
return Web::view('Books/show', ['book' => $book]);
return Web::view('Books/missing', ['message' => 'No such book'], 404);
return Web::redirect('/books');
return Web::redirect('https://checkout.stripe.com/...', 303);
return Web::json(['enrolled' => true], 201);
return Web::text('ok')->header('Cache-Control', 'no-store');
```

<a name="action"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Action

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Action
```

Source: [framework/core/Action.php:27](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Action.php#L27)

Class Action (2.21.0)
Route::action('/connect', 'cloud_connect') answers a request with a capability declared webOnly: true, for what a
page or a form cannot say: a sign-in between two sites, a session that decides where to go, a gate, a payment page.
1. access: the 'signedIn', 'level', 'comeBack' and 'visitorsOnly' options of Route::page
2. the capability is called with the query string or the form, and the route variables (which win), as the person who sent it, with its rules, permissions and audit log like any capability
3. its answer goes to the browser: a Caligrafy\Web (a view, a redirect, JSON, text), or JSON of the plain data A JSON call needs the page's X-CSRF-Token or an API token, signed in or not ([ERROR 1004], 401)
4. a refusal it does not answer itself is treated as in Route::form: invalid input or a conflict goes back with errors(), old() and flash('error'); a visitor goes to sign in; forbidden is 403, anything else 404. JSON requests get the REST error.
Unlike every other capability, it may read the session and the request and may sign people in, and a GET may change
data: so a webOnly capability is reachable through Route::action only, never through REST, MCP, the JS client,
Route::page, Route::form or a controller.

+ [`Action::handle()`](#action-handle)
+ [`Action::answer()`](#action-answer)

<a name="form"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Form

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Form
```

Source: [framework/core/Form.php:29](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Form.php#L29)

Class Form (2.19.0)
Route::form('/books', 'create_book', ['success' =&gt; '/books/{id}', 'flash' =&gt; 'Book added']) answers the form's POST
(or its PUT / DELETE through \_method) with a capability, without a controller:
1. the CSRF token of the form is checked by the request, as for every form (error 3000, 403)
2. the capability is called with the form fields, the files of its `file` inputs (Uploads) and the route variables (which win), as the person who sent the form (Context::fromRequest(..., 'web'))
3. success: a redirect to 'success' (a path whose {placeholders} are filled from the result, then from the route variables, or a callable($result) returning the path; without it, back to the form), with the 'flash' message (also with placeholders) for flash('success')
4. invalid input (or a conflict): back to the form ('back', else the Referer of this site, else /) with the field errors, the message and the old input for the next request: errors($field), old($field), flash('error')
5. a visitor where the capability needs someone: to the sign-in page ('signIn', default /login) when Auth is active, else 403; forbidden: 403 (error 1006); not found: 404 (error 1005)
A JSON request (Accept: application/json) gets the REST answer instead of redirects: {"data": ...} with 200 (201 for a
POST that changes data), or {"error": ...} with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422. Sent with the session cookie, it needs the
X-CSRF-Token header, as REST.

### Constants

+ `SECRET = '/pass|secret|token|card|cvc|cvv|iban/i'`: fields never kept as old input

<a name="download"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Download

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Download
```

Source: [framework/core/Download.php:32](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Download.php#L32)

Class Download (2.19.0)
Route::download('/books.csv', 'list_books', ['as' =&gt; 'csv', 'filename' =&gt; 'books.csv']) answers a GET with the result
of a read-only capability as an attachment, without a controller:

- inputs: the query string and the route variables (which win), as the person who opens the link (Context::fromRequest(..., 'web')); the capability must be readOnly (a link must not change data)
- 'as' =&gt; 'csv' (default): RFC 4180 (CRLF, fields with a comma, a quote or a line break in double quotes, quotes doubled), UTF-8, the header row from the first row's keys; 'bom' =&gt; true starts the file with a UTF-8 BOM (Excel); text cells that start with = + - @ or a tab are prefixed with ' so that spreadsheets do not run them as formulas ('formulas' =&gt; true keeps them as they are); arrays in a cell are written as JSON, booleans as true / false. 'as' =&gt; 'json': the result, pretty-printed
- 'as' =&gt; 'zip' (2.22.0): the files the capability lists, in one ZIP archive streamed from a temporary file. Each item is a path (the file keeps its name) or ['file' =&gt; path, 'name' =&gt; 'folder/name in the archive']; a page of paginate() gives its rows. Paths are relative to 'root', a folder of the project (default 'public/uploads'): a file outside it, or missing, is left out, so a link never reaches other files. Duplicate names get " (2)". Images, video, audio and archives are stored as they are, other files compressed. No file at all: 404 (error 1005). Needs the PHP zip extension (in Caligrafy's Docker images and on Caligrafy Cloud)
- 'filename': a name, or a callable($result, $input) returning one (default: the capability's name)
- refusals as Route::page: a visitor is sent to sign in when Auth is active, else 403 (error 1006); forbidden 403; anything else 404 (error 1005)

### Constants

+ `FORMATS = array('csv', 'json', 'zip')`
+ `STORED = ...`

<a name="webhook"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Webhook

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Webhook
```

Source: [framework/core/Webhook.php:24](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Webhook.php#L24)

Class Webhook (2.19.0)
Route::webhook('/stripe/events', 'record_payment', ['verify' =&gt; 'stripe']) answers the POSTs of another service with
a capability, without a controller:

- no CSRF token (the sender has no session): the signature of the body proves who sent it. 'verify' is required: 'stripe' checks the Stripe-Signature header with \Stripe\Webhook::constructEvent and the secret in the variable 'secret_env' names (default STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), with 'tolerance' seconds (default 300); a callable function (string $rawBody, array $headers): bool checks anything else (headers with lower-case names)
- the raw body (php://input) must be JSON; the capability gets ['event' =&gt; the decoded body], as the system (Context::system('webhook', $path)): declare public $rules = ['event' =&gt; 'required']
- answers: 200 {"received": true}; 400 for a bad signature or a body that is not JSON; the status of a ServiceError; 500 for anything else (written to the PHP error log)

### Public properties

+ `public static $logger = null`: callable|null replaces error_log() (tests)

### Methods

+ [`Webhook::handle()`](#webhook-handle)
+ [`Webhook::process()`](#webhook-process)
+ [`Webhook::verify()`](#webhook-verify)

<a name="uploads"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Uploads

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Uploads
```

Source: [framework/core/Uploads.php:28](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Uploads.php#L28)

Class Uploads (2.19.0)
A capability declares a file input with the rule `file`, an optional allow-list and an optional maximum size:

```
public $rules = ['cover' => 'required|file|extension,png;jpg|max_size,2mb'];
```

- web pages (Route::form) and REST (Route::capability, Route::capabilities) take the field from $_FILES once the caller is allowed to call the capability, check it (one file, the allow-list - never an executable type, see isAllowedUpload() - and the size), save it in public/uploads under a new random name with uploadFile() (the name the client sent is never used) and give handle() the saved file's public URL, a string. A value sent in that field without a file is dropped. The saved file is deleted when the call fails afterwards.
- MCP and the command line cannot send files: the field is a URL or a path string; its extension is checked against the allow-list.

The file rules (file, extension, max_size, required_file) are never given to GUMP: Service::validate() strips them.
A field with required_file (or required) and no file is invalid: 'The &lt;Field&gt; field needs a file' (2.19.1).
Without `extension` the allow-list is DEFAULT_UPLOAD_EXTENSIONS.

### Constants

+ `RULES = array('file', 'extension', 'max_size', 'required_file')`

<a name="throttle"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Throttle

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Throttle
```

Source: [framework/core/Throttle.php:19](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Throttle.php#L19)

Class Throttle (2.19.0)

```
$throttle = new Throttle(5, 900);          // 5 failures within 15 minutes lock the key for the rest of them
if ($throttle->locked($key)) ...; $throttle->fail($key); $throttle->clear($key);
```

The counts are kept in the Cache (CACHE_STORE: the caligrafy_cache table or a private folder, shared by every
session, so that a new cookie does not start again), or in the session when the cache is off.
Each failure keeps the count for $seconds more.

### Public properties

+ `public $max`: int
+ `public $seconds`: int

Sends an error response: HTTP status code and the error text (HTML requests) or
{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}} (requests that want JSON)
Framework errors keep their message. Other exceptions caught by the application keep theirs too
unless $hideUnknown is true (uncaught exceptions), in which case the message is only shown when APP_DEBUG is true

**Parameters**

+ `$hideUnknown` `bool`, default `false`: hides the message of errors that are not framework errors unless APP_DEBUG is true

<a name="flash"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Flash

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Flash
```

Source: [framework/core/Flash.php:20](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Flash.php#L20)

Class Flash (2.19.0)
Route::form() puts the field errors, the old input and a message here before it redirects; the page of the next
request reads them with the view helpers errors($field), old($field) and flash($key), then they are gone.
Route::run() ages them when there are some: what the previous request put becomes this request's, and leaves the
session (without Route::run, the first read does).

Kept in $_SESSION['__flash'] as ['errors' =&gt; [field =&gt; message], 'old' =&gt; [field =&gt; value], 'messages' =&gt; [key =&gt; text]].

### Constants

+ `KEY = '__flash'`

+ [`Flash::age()`](#flash-age)
+ [`Flash::put()`](#flash-put)
+ [`Flash::message()`](#flash-message)
+ [`Flash::get()`](#flash-get)
+ [`Flash::reset()`](#flash-reset)

<a name="context"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Context

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Context
```

Source: [framework/core/Context.php:23](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Context.php#L23)

Class Context
Built by the channel adapters (web pages, REST, MCP, CLI) and read by the services: a service never looks at the
request, the session or the headers itself.

The actor is one of:

- user: a signed-in user (session), or the owner of a token
- token: a personal access token (Tokens), with its scopes
- key: the legacy API key (every generated key is the same key: full access, as before 2.1)
- cli: a script or the command line (full access); a scheduled job is a system context on this channel
- guest: nobody: only public capabilities

### Constants

+ `CHANNELS = array('web', 'rest', 'mcp', 'cli')`

### Public properties

+ `public static $levelAttribute = 'permissions'`: Name of the users column that holds the permission level compared with a capability's level (Auth::guard)
+ `public $channel`: string web, rest, mcp or cli
+ `public $viaAction = false`: bool the call comes from Route::action() (2.21.0): the only way to a webOnly capability
+ `public $user`: object|null the user model (signed in, or the owner of the token)
+ `public $token`: array|null the token row (id, name, scopes, user_id...)

### Methods

+ [`->__construct()`](#context-construct)
+ [`Context::cli()`](#context-cli)
+ [`Context::local()`](#context-local)
+ [`Context::system()`](#context-system)
+ [`Context::guest()`](#context-guest)
+ [`Context::forToken()`](#context-fortoken)
+ [`Context::fromRequest()`](#context-fromrequest)
+ [`->authenticated()`](#context-authenticated)
+ [`->allows()`](#context-allows)
+ [`->level()`](#context-level)
+ [`->userId()`](#context-userid)
+ [`->actorType()`](#context-actortype)
+ [`->actorId()`](#context-actorid)

<a name="context-allows"></a>
#### `->allows()`

```php
public function allows($scope, $level = 0)
```

Whether this context may use a capability that needs a scope and a minimum user level

- the CLI and the legacy key: always
- a token: it must grant the scope, and its owner (if any) must have the level
- a signed-in user: the level (users have every scope their level allows)

**Parameters**

+ `$scope` `string`: e.g. books:write ('' = no scope needed)
+ `$level` `int`, default `0`: minimum value of the users permission column (0 = any signed-in user)

Source: [framework/core/Context.php:163](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Context.php#L163)
